event: Russia invades Ukraine. European gas and oil prices jump within days.
The European Commission launches REPowerEU, a plan to stop buying Russian fossil fuels.
The UK brings in the Energy Profits Levy: an extra 25% tax on oil and gas producers' profits.
European gas hits an all-time high of €319 per megawatt-hour on the Dutch TTF market.
Explosions wreck the Nord Stream pipelines under the Baltic Sea.
EU emergency rules take effect: a 'solidarity contribution' of at least 33% on fossil fuel firms' extra profits, and a €180 per MWh cap on some power producers' revenues.
EU countries agree a gas price cap: the market correction mechanism at €180 per MWh.
Russian gas stops flowing to Europe through Ukraine as the transit deal expires.
BP cuts its yearly low-carbon spending to $1.5 to $2 billion and raises oil and gas spending to about $10 billion.
EU countries give final approval to a step-by-step ban on Russian gas: LNG from the start of 2027, pipeline gas from autumn 2027.
The United States and Israel strike Iran. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz slows to a near standstill.
QatarEnergy halts production at Ras Laffan after Iranian drone attacks. European gas prices jump 46% in a day, to €46.52 per MWh.
With storage only about 30% full, the Commission tells EU countries they can lower their gas storage target from 90% to 80%.
A ceasefire is announced. Oil falls 13% in a day.
The Commission relaxes state aid rules so governments can help households and industry with bills, and allows further windfall taxes.
Tankers move through the Strait of Hormuz again, and oil falls back to where it was in February.
Fighting starts again. The strait is 'effectively closed', Qatar's LNG is still offline and European gas tops €70 per MWh.
The United States announces an 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine. Ukraine reports new Russian strikes within days.
Brent oil falls back below $100 a barrel, after averaging $124 in October.
